topics.definition: An Operating System (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides services to programs.
tips: Acts as an interface between users and hardware.

topics.definition: Operating systems evolved from simple batch systems to modern multitasking and distributed systems.
tips: Modern OS supports multitasking and networking.

topics.definition: Common types include Batch, Time-Sharing, Distributed, Real-Time, Network and Mobile operating systems.
tips: Different OS types suit different applications.

topics.definition: The OS manages processes, memory, files, devices, security and users.
tips: Resource management is the primary role of an OS.

topics.definition: User mode runs applications with limited privileges, while kernel mode has full access to system resources.
OS architecture defines how system components are organized.
tips: Each architecture has advantages and trade-offs.

topics.definition: Popular operating systems include Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS.
tips: Choose an OS based on your needs.

topics.definition: Keep the OS updated, secure and backed up for reliable performance.
tips: Use strong passwords and regular updates.
